rationale: The race data shows the robot still fails to complete the tracks, with one line loss event per run and off-track termination around 60% progress. The rear sensors moved further back (y from -0.01 to -0.02) and the wheel track increased from 0.16 to 0.17 as requested, aiming to improve early turn detection and lateral stability. However, the controller still experiences line loss and off-track failures, indicating the controller parameters need tuning to exploit the geometry changes. I increased the base_speed slightly from 0.14 to 0.145 to improve progress, and adjusted the PID gains to kp=0.20, ki=0.025, kd=0.04 to provide stronger and more responsive control, helping reduce line loss and off-track events. Sensor weights are slightly adjusted to emphasize the central and rear sensors more, aiding in earlier detection of line deviations. The line_loss strategy remains 'search_left' as it suits the sensor layout. The observation request is extended to include all previously requested measurements plus steering_oscillation and control_effort to better monitor controller behavior and stability in future races. These changes aim to improve line following robustness, reduce line loss events, and increase completion and progress metrics on both tracks.
